title: OpenAI Scales Git for Coding Agents with Pando
gist: OpenAI built Pando, a Git-compatible backend that relaxes repository-wide consistency to scale for Codex-driven coding-agent load; it cut median push latency ~80%, serves nearly a petabyte of Git data daily, and contrasts with Anthropic's Scion, which replaces Git's model with a server-side service.

insights.claim: OpenAI's Pando Git backend now powers all development in OpenAI's monorepo and serves nearly a petabyte of Git data per day, load OpenAI attributes to Codex-driven development.
insights.speaker: Eran Stiller
insights.so_what: Coding agents multiply load on dev infrastructure (source control, CI) — a second-order demand driver for dev-infra vendors.

insights.claim: Each agent-driven push can trigger multiple CI jobs that all fetch the same history, compounding Git server load under coding-agent workloads.
insights.speaker: Eran Stiller
insights.so_what: CI and artifact-delivery infrastructure scale super-linearly with agent adoption.

insights.claim: OpenAI reports Pando cut median push latency by nearly 80% by coordinating branch updates independently and reusing stored packfiles across fetches; it went into production in April 2026.
insights.speaker: Eran Stiller
insights.so_what: Legacy Git hosting architectures may be inadequate for agent-scale repos — pressure on GitHub/GitLab-style backends.

insights.claim: Pando provides causal consistency with serialisable per-reference updates and read-your-own-write consistency, but no repository-wide snapshot across branches, removing a shared coordination point for unrelated pushes.
insights.speaker: Eran Stiller
insights.so_what: Relaxing global consistency is the key lever for scaling agent-era infra — a reusable architectural pattern.
insights.locator: OpenAI refers to this as causal consistency

insights.claim: Pando validates pushed packfiles while streaming them to immutable blob storage without unpacking, and advertises only a trunk branch as base so packs can be reused, trading extra bandwidth for reusability.
insights.speaker: Eran Stiller
insights.so_what: Shifts cost from compute to storage/bandwidth — favourable for object-storage consumption.
insights.locator: Rather than replace Git's client and protocol

insights.claim: Pando uses Git's packfile-uri capability to return download links served by Express, a regional pack-delivery cache with cache-hit rates above 99% and tests saturating 10 Gbps links.
insights.speaker: Eran Stiller
insights.so_what: Caching/CDN-style delivery becomes central to source control at agent scale.

insights.claim: Pando's background compaction groups packs into geometrically sized covers, resembling log-structured merge-tree compaction, which improves compression and serves as a skip-list-like index for fetch planning.
insights.speaker: Eran Stiller
insights.so_what: Database storage techniques are migrating into source-control infrastructure.

insights.claim: Anthropic's Scion takes the opposite approach to OpenAI's Pando: it replaces Git's model with changesets and server-side commits, merges and rebases, assumes an online client, and uses sparse or virtualised checkouts, whereas Pando preserves Git's object model and client workflows.
insights.speaker: Eran Stiller
insights.so_what: Frontier labs are diverging on whether to keep Git — watch which model incumbents like GitHub adopt.
insights.locator: The design contrasts with Anthropic's Scion

insights.claim: OpenAI's Pando and Anthropic's Scion results are not directly comparable: OpenAI reports push latency, while Anthropic reports checkout speedups and infrastructure reductions versus its prior Git setup.
insights.speaker: Eran Stiller
insights.so_what: Avoid headline comparisons between the two systems' performance claims.
insights.locator: Both systems make use of immutable data

insights.claim: Despite Git compatibility, OpenAI had to deploy Pando as a read/write-through proxy, migrate clients in phases, move hundreds of integrations, and ship its own Git build supporting parallel pack download and indexing.
insights.speaker: Eran Stiller
insights.so_what: Source-control migrations remain costly even when protocol-compatible — sticky incumbency for Git hosts.
insights.locator: Git compatibility did not eliminate migration work

insights.claim: Architects face two separate decisions: which source-control operations belong on the server, and which consistency and transfer guarantees their workloads actually need.
insights.speaker: Eran Stiller
insights.so_what: A useful lens for evaluating next-gen dev-infra vendors.
insights.locator: For the architects, it's a case
